author: Lucas Downey
title: Searching for Value | Investopedia
text:
By Lucas Downey from Investopedia | December 17, 2018 — 9:00 AM EST Sponsored Content Investopedia is paid to republish articles or advertorials written by other investing and financial information publishers across the industry.
Lucas Downey writes from the perspective of a position trader. Read more on different trading types here .
Last week, indexes fell hard. The Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) is now -7.84% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and DJIA ETF (DIA) are both negative for 2018, at -1.82% and -0.88% respectively. It's been rough going.
The key here is to pay attention to the data. For weeks, that data has signaled that investors should focus on yielding stocks for safety. Apartment Investment and Management Co. (AIV), Xcel Energy (XEL) and Dominion Energy (D) fit the bill for defensive plays. Also, with falling yields, banks should continue to suffer (even though they are oversold). Three banks that have been showing large selling this year are: Morgan Stanley (MS), Bank of America (BAC) and Capital One Financial (COF). Finally, three tech stocks have been showing value: Apple (AAPL), Broadcom (AVGO) and NVIDIA (NVDA).
Source: FactSet Unusual Selling Approaches Extreme Levels
Markets fell last week, as unusual selling signals outnumbered buying signals by a wide margin. As you can see below, there were 69 signals of potential buying versus 702 of selling. A normal average is 1.5 buys to sells, so this level of selling is on the extreme end. The blue arrow below denotes the weekly signals:
Source: www.mapsignals.com
To take it a step further, the chart below shows buying and selling by sector. The main takeaways are: buying was seen in utilities and big selling was seen across financials, energy, industrials and consumer discretionary. The potential buying and selling is shown below by sector in green and red bars:
Mapping this data over five weeks, we can see that selling is gaining because the lower line is falling. The line in the bottom chart rising out of the green area has historically been a bullish sign for markets. However, the line is heading lower again, so we could soon reach oversold (idicated by the green area). The coming week could see heavier selling, which may give us a buy signal if the ratio touches green.
Source: www.mapsignals.com One Real Estate Stock Shows Unusual Buying
I’ll remain interested in real estate names as long as the trend for the sector is higher. This low-yield environment is advantageous for REITs . Apartment Investment and Management Co. (AIV) triggered an unusual buy signal last week. This fits with what we saw the prior week, so the trend is your friend in the real estate space. Source: www.mapsignals.com Utility Names Alert Bullish Activity
Along the same theme for a low-yield environment, utilities are known for high payouts and safety. Xcel Energy, Inc. (XEL) and Dominion Energy, Inc. (D) have been leaders in the utilities sector. This sector was a bright spot last week as markets were in turmoil. I expect this group to perform well if more selling in the overall market takes place.
Source: www.mapsignals.com Banks On the Chopping Block
Lower yields, slowing growth and global pessimism have kept the financials sector on the bottom rung for much of 2018. Last week , I discussed how a flatting yield curve is bad for banks. The trend of selling banks is still in play: last week saw very aggressive selling in the space. Three financial names I’ve been watching the last couple of months are Morgan Stanley (MS), Bank of America (BAC) and Capital One Financial (COF). The sector has been out of favor for much of 2018 and until the space sees a slowing of declines on higher volumes, I’ll pass.
Source: www.mapsignals.com Looking for Value
Yes, markets are heading lower; but this is the time to focus on prior leading stocks that have fallen out of favor. Technology has been wrecked, but since I’m longer-term in nature, I strive to do is grab “great” stocks on sale. Apple Inc. (AAPL), Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) and NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) all look to show value. Apple and Broadcom both sport growing dividends and sales, while NVIDIA has hit roadblocks on growth. As I’ve heard great investors say, “sometimes you need to feel the fear and do it anyway.”
Source: www.mapsignals.com The Takeaway
My stance is long-term bullish and short-term defensive. Dividend-rich names like AIV, XEL and D are seeing buying pressure for a short-term lift. Financials still see selling, which makes the case to steer clear until clarity comes for the space. Finally, three value, tech stocks are likely prudent buys for the long-term investor (AAPL, AVGO, NVDA).
Disclosure: the author holds no positions in AIV, XEL, D, MS, BAC, COF, AAPL, AVGO, & NVDA at the time of publication.
